articles.title: Authors' Response to AI-Based Reviews: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study
articles.summary: arXiv:2605.16623v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Background: Large language models are increasingly used to assist scholarly peer review, but there is limited evidence about how authors judge their feedback and use it to revise their papers. Methods: We studied authors' experiences of receiving an auxiliary AI review alongside human reviews in three computer-science cohorts: LifeCLEF 2025, LifeCLEF 2026, and CVWW 2026. articles.title: SST-Guard: Detecting and Characterizing Server-Side Google Analytics in the Wild
articles.summary: arXiv:2604.27497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As web browsers increasingly implement anti-tracking features, the web tracking ecosystem has been shifting from the client-side to the server-side. Instead of sending requests directly to the tracker's endpoint, server-side tracking (SST) sends tracking requests to publisher-controlled or intermediary endpoints that then forward the information to trackers from the server-side. articles.title: Polar: A Benchmark for Evaluating Political Bias in LLMs
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.12922v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Political bias in large language models (LLMs) is increasingly significant, but difficult to measure reproducibly across political and linguistic contexts. We introduce Polar, a 4,026-instance multiple-choice benchmark that measures political bias through option-level likelihoods rather than prompt-based generation. Polar covers two ideological axes and eight issue categories derived from the Manifesto Project, and evaluates models in parallel across U.S. and South Korean political contexts.
